data.name: Atooms to Moolecules Demo
data.detailed_description:
Atooms to Moolecules is a chemistry based puzzle game. In this game you are in a Chemistry lab, your task is to solve different puzzles. You can arrange atoms to make ring, linear, small or big molecules and have fun with them. The game is played in different lab equipment. Don’t start wondering about your elementary chemistry concepts, you really don’t need them to master this game. Just explore the lab and solve the puzzles.

Key Features:

  • Adventure Mode: Adventure Mode is the primary mode, and it allows you to learn the ways to make molecules. Adventure Mode is divided into 8 stages.
  • Lab Setup Mode: Lab Setup is a sand box mode where you can setup a lab of yourself.
  • Scoring: You can grab some extra points with the help of Ring Bonus and Hydrogen Bonus.

reviews.review:
Horrible. Chemical reactions aren't real, many impossible molecules are allowed (e.g. O6, N4, C4). The lab equipment just gets in the way, and you aren't given any understanding of the scoring system, nor of how quickly certain molecules affect the temperature or pH. Xs are horribly annoying as they can only bind to one other "atoom", and do not exist anyway. The structures are also apparently arbitrary, and do not follow known bond angles. pH is not affected by the concentration of hydroxide ions. Radioactive particles are far too large in comparison with atom sizes. Molecules can spontaneously gain momentum, violating the laws of physics. Difficulty curve is far too easy, save for the last level, which is much more difficult in comparison to everything else.

Thankfully it's free, but I'd much rather play SpaceChem or Sokobond, as those appear to actually have accurate, playable content.

I'm not sure if one can change one's review after it's published, but if many of these inaccuracies are fixed, then I shall amend this review as required.
